faqs.question: What is liquid wrapping?
faqs.answer: Liquid wrapping is a sprayed-on, peelable coating that changes the color of your vehicle. It goes on like paint and comes off like a wrap — so you get a smooth, even finish that follows every curve, vent and body line, with none of the seams or lifted edges you get from vinyl.

faqs.question: Will it damage my factory paint?
faqs.answer: No. The coating bonds to the surface, not into it. When it is removed, it peels away in sheets and leaves the original paint exactly as it was underneath. Factory paint in sound condition is actually protected from sun, light scratches and road debris while the wrap is on.

faqs.question: How is this different from vinyl wrap?
faqs.answer: Vinyl is a film that gets stretched over panels, so complex curves, deep vents and recessed areas can be tough to cover cleanly. Liquid wrap is sprayed, so it coats those areas evenly with no relief cuts, no seams and no edges to lift. It is also easier to repair — a damaged area can be spot-treated instead of re-wrapping a whole panel.

faqs.question: What colors and finishes can I get?
faqs.answer: Solid gloss, satin and matte are always available. Beyond that we can do metallics, pearls, color-shift, candies, fades and multi-tone layouts. If you have a specific color in mind — including an OEM code from another vehicle — bring it to us and we will work out the closest match.

faqs.question: Can you wrap only part of the car?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Wheels, roof, hood, mirror caps, grille, badges and chrome trim are all common standalone jobs. A lot of customers start with a chrome delete or wheels before committing to a full color change.

faqs.question: How long does a liquid wrap last?
faqs.answer: With normal driving and reasonable care, expect several years of service life. Garage-kept vehicles and lighter-duty use go longer; daily drivers parked outside year-round will show wear sooner. Higher-tier packages add build coats and a protective top coat, which is where most of the extra longevity comes from.

faqs.question: How do I wash it?
faqs.answer: Hand wash with a pH-neutral soap and a soft mitt, and dry with a clean microfiber. Avoid automatic brush washes, and keep high-pressure nozzles a reasonable distance back — especially near edges. Do not use aggressive solvents, bug-and-tar removers or polishing compounds on the finish.

faqs.question: What if it gets scratched or chipped?
faqs.answer: That is one of the real advantages of a sprayed finish. Damaged areas can usually be scuffed and re-coated in place, blending into the surrounding panel rather than requiring the whole panel to be redone. Bring it by and we will take a look.

faqs.question: How soon can I drive it and wash it?
faqs.answer: You can drive the vehicle as soon as we hand it back. The coating continues to cure over the following days, so hold off on washing for about a week and keep it out of automatic washes entirely. We will give you specific timing at pickup.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on the size of the vehicle, the condition of the existing paint, the finish you choose and how much disassembly the job needs. Send us a note through the contact form with your vehicle and the look you are after, and we will get you a real number rather than a guess.

faqs.question: How long will my vehicle be at the shop?
faqs.answer: Most single-color jobs are a two to four day turnaround. Metallic, chrome and pearl work runs three to five days. Full custom projects are typically one to three weeks depending on complexity and disassembly.

faqs.question: Does my paint need to be perfect first?
faqs.answer: It does not need to be perfect, but it does need to be sound. Clear coat that is already peeling, flaking or lifting will telegraph through and can come off with the wrap later. We will inspect the vehicle before quoting and tell you honestly what we are working with.

faqs.question: How do I book?
faqs.answer: Fill out the quote form on the contact page with your vehicle and the service you are interested in — that is the fastest way to get a response. You are also welcome to call or text us during business hours.
